guide.title: Oxygen & Ventilation Skills
guide.lead: Oxygen is a drug: give enough to reach the target, not more. SpO₂ tells you about oxygenation; capnography tells you about ventilation, circulation and tube position. Know how long your cylinder will last before you need it.

steps.title: Formula
steps.text: Minutes = (gauge pressure − 200 psi reserve) × cylinder factor ÷ flow (L/min).

steps.title: Example
steps.text: E cylinder at 2000 psi, 15 L/min: (2000 − 200) × 0.28 ÷ 15 ≈ 34 minutes.

sections.title: Oxygen safety
items: No smoking or open flames; no oil, grease or petroleum products on fittings or skin
Secure cylinders: a broken valve turns them into missiles
Open valves slowly; replace at 200 psi

sections.title: When SpO₂ misleads
items: Poor perfusion, cold hands, movement: no reading or wrong
Severe anaemia: normal % but little oxygen carried
Dark nail polish and darker skin can overestimate saturation

sections.title: When to assist ventilation
items: Respiratory rate below 8/min or too shallow
Exhaustion or falling consciousness with rising CO₂

quiz.q: E cylinder at 1600 psi, 15 L/min. Minutes left (keeping a 200 psi reserve)?
ETCO₂ stays at 8 mmHg during CPR. Most likely?
options: Compressions aren't generating enough output: improve them

quiz.q: COPD patient on a non-rebreather: SpO₂ 100%, ETCO₂ 68 mmHg, drowsy. This is:
options: Good oxygenation but severe hypoventilation: titrate oxygen down and assist breathing

quiz.q: House-fire victim: confused, headache, SpO₂ 99%. Why distrust the SpO₂?
options: Pulse oximeters read carbon monoxide as oxygen

quiz.q: Sudden sustained ETCO₂ rise during CPR suggests:
Cylinder factor for an E cylinder:
Assist ventilation when the adult respiratory rate is below:
quiz.explanation: Also apnoea, agonal breathing or exhaustion.

flashcards.question: Oxygen cylinders
flashcards.answer: D: portable. E: most common portable on ambulances. M and H: large onboard supply. Full at about 2000 psi; change at 200 psi.

flashcards.question: Cylinder duration
flashcards.answer: (Pressure − 200 psi) × factor ÷ flow. Factors: D 0.16, E 0.28, M 1.56, H 3.14. E at 2000 psi, 15 L/min ≈ 34 minutes.

flashcards.question: Oxygen safety
flashcards.answer: No smoking, no oil or grease, secure cylinders, open slowly, keep away from heat, replace at 200 psi.

flashcards.question: Pulse oximetry errors
flashcards.answer: CO (falsely normal), poor perfusion, motion, severe anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, nail polish; can overestimate in darker skin.

flashcards.question: ETCO₂ values
flashcards.answer: Normal 35–45 mmHg. Low: hyperventilation, low output, PE. High: hypoventilation. Sudden rise in CPR: ROSC.

flashcards.question: Capnography and tube position
flashcards.answer: A sustained waveform confirms tracheal placement. No waveform: oesophageal until proven otherwise.

flashcards.question: Complications of positive pressure ventilation
flashcards.answer: Gastric inflation (vomiting, aspiration), lower venous return (hypotension), barotrauma (pneumothorax).

flashcards.question: Indications for assisted ventilation
flashcards.answer: Apnoea, agonal breathing, RR below 8/min or too shallow, hypoxia despite high-flow oxygen, exhaustion or falling consciousness.

critical.scenario: CPR with a supraglottic airway: ETCO₂ has been 12–15 mmHg; it suddenly rises to 42 mmHg and stays there.
critical.question: Meaning and action?

options.t: Likely ROSC: check the pulse and rhythm; if a pulse is present start post-arrest care

critical.explanation: ETCO₂ is the earliest sign of ROSC.

critical.scenario: COPD on home oxygen 2 L/min: SpO₂ 86%. A first responder put her on 15 L/min; now SpO₂ 99%, drowsy, ETCO₂ 72 mmHg.
critical.question: Cause and response?

options.t: CO₂ retention from excess oxygen: titrate to 88–92%, assist ventilation or CPAP/NIV per protocol, monitor ETCO₂

critical.explanation: SpO₂ 99% is too high for her.
critical.kpi: Titrates oxygen in a CO₂-retaining patient

critical.scenario: Long rural transport with a patient needing 15 L/min. Your portable E cylinder reads 1000 psi.
critical.question: What do you do?

options.t: Calculate: (1000 − 200) × 0.28 ÷ 15 ≈ 15 minutes – switch to the onboard supply before moving and bring a spare
Lower the flow to make it last regardless of need

critical.kpi: Calculates oxygen cylinder duration for transport
